::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 2nd 1877  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 15
:::

Dear [Mr Craik](people/person_379.qmd),

Thinking it over I had rather, since you are so kind, keep [the £200](organizations/other_160.qmd) on credit, as I think the receipt for /this\\ next year, considering the [Cameos](cmy_books/cmybook_124.qmd) and the two French histories must a good deal more than cover that sum, and it is convenient to me to have it in hand just now[^1]

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The 'two French histories' were the *History of France*, in the 'Historical Course for Schools' which E. A. Freeman, the series editor, was making her rewrite, and which was not actually published until 1879; and the *History of France* (1878) which she was contributing to the 'History Primers' series edited by J. R. Green. The former was aimed at older children, and had ten chapters rather than eight.
